subject: TUR
name: Türkiye
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: The Neolithic town of Çatalhöyük
claims.summary: On the Konya plain, the streetless settlement of Çatalhöyük flourished for over a millennium (c. 7100–5700 BCE), one of the world's best-preserved Neolithic towns, with roof-access houses and elaborate wall art.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-7100bce-the-neolithic-town-of-catalhoyuk, claim TL:TUR:event:7100bce:the-neolithic-town-of-catalhoyuk, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hattusa becomes the Hittite capital
claims.summary: King Hattusilis I established Hattusa in north-central Anatolia as the capital of the Hittite kingdom, the seat of a Bronze Age empire that would rival Egypt.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1650bce-hattusa-becomes-the-hittite-capital, claim TL:TUR:event:1650bce:hattusa-becomes-the-hittite-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Kadesh and the Hittite–Egyptian treaty
claims.summary: The Hittites under Muwatalli II fought Ramesses II of Egypt at Kadesh; the conflict ended in one of history's earliest surviving peace treaties between the two empires.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1274bce-battle-of-kadesh-and-the-hittite-egyptian-treaty, claim TL:TUR:event:1274bce:battle-of-kadesh-and-the-hittite-egyptian-treaty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Troy of the Iliad
claims.summary: The fortified city at Hisarlık (Troy VI–VII) corresponds to the era of the Trojan War remembered in Homer's Iliad; the layered ruins were excavated from 1870 and inscribed by UNESCO in 1998.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1250bce-troy-of-the-iliad, claim TL:TUR:event:1250bce:troy-of-the-iliad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bronze Age collapse
claims.summary: Around 1200–1180 BCE the Hittite state and Hattusa were destroyed amid the wider collapse of eastern Mediterranean civilisations, ending Anatolia's first great imperial age.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1180bce-bronze-age-collapse, claim TL:TUR:event:1180bce:bronze-age-collapse, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Lydia and Croesus
claims.summary: The wealthy Lydian kingdom of western Anatolia, credited with pioneering coined money, fell to Cyrus the Great of Persia, bringing Anatolia under Persian rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-547bce-fall-of-lydia-and-croesus, claim TL:TUR:event:547bce:fall-of-lydia-and-croesus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constantine refounds Constantinople
claims.summary: Constantine the Great dedicated the rebuilt city of Byzantium as Constantinople, a new Christian capital on the Bosporus that would anchor the Roman and then Byzantine state for over a millennium.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-330-constantine-refounds-constantinople, claim TL:TUR:event:330:constantine-refounds-constantinople, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Justinian completes the Hagia Sophia
claims.summary: Emperor Justinian I inaugurated the great domed church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, the masterpiece of Byzantine architecture and for centuries the largest cathedral in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-537-justinian-completes-the-hagia-sophia, claim TL:TUR:event:537:justinian-completes-the-hagia-sophia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Manzikert
claims.summary: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated and captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV at Manzikert, breaking Byzantine control of the interior and opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1071-battle-of-manzikert, claim TL:TUR:event:1071:battle-of-manzikert, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sultanate of Rûm at Konya
claims.summary: Seljuk Turks established the Sultanate of Rûm in Anatolia, with Konya as its centre, fostering a rich Islamic culture associated with the mystic poet Rumi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1077-sultanate-of-rum-at-konya, claim TL:TUR:event:1077:sultanate-of-rum-at-konya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the Ottoman emirate
claims.summary: Osman I, leader of a frontier emirate in north-western Anatolia, is traditionally regarded as founder of the Ottoman dynasty around 1299, giving his name to the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1299-foundation-of-the-ottoman-emirate, claim TL:TUR:event:1299:foundation-of-the-ottoman-emirate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Kosovo
claims.summary: Ottoman forces under Murad I defeated a Serbian-led coalition at Kosovo, cementing Ottoman dominance in the Balkans even as Murad died on the field.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1389-battle-of-kosovo, claim TL:TUR:event:1389:battle-of-kosovo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Ankara and the Interregnum
claims.summary: Timur (Tamerlane) crushed and captured Sultan Bayezid I at Ankara, plunging the Ottoman state into a decade of civil war before it recovered.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1402-battle-of-ankara-and-the-interregnum, claim TL:TUR:event:1402:battle-of-ankara-and-the-interregnum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Constantinople
claims.summary: After a 53-day siege, Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire; the city became the Ottoman capital and Hagia Sophia was converted to a mosque.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1453-fall-of-constantinople, claim TL:TUR:event:1453:fall-of-constantinople, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Süleyman the Magnificent
claims.summary: Süleyman I presided over the Ottoman Empire at its territorial and cultural height, from Hungary to the Arab lands, codifying law and patronising the architecture of Sinan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1520-reign-of-suleyman-the-magnificent, claim TL:TUR:event:1520:reign-of-suleyman-the-magnificent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Siege of Vienna
claims.summary: Ottoman armies under Süleyman besieged Vienna, marking the high-water mark of Ottoman expansion into central Europe before withdrawing.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1529-first-siege-of-vienna, claim TL:TUR:event:1529:first-siege-of-vienna, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Karlowitz
claims.summary: After the failed 1683 siege of Vienna, the Treaty of Karlowitz ceded Hungary and other lands to the Habsburgs, the first major Ottoman territorial retreat in Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1699-treaty-of-karlowitz, claim TL:TUR:event:1699:treaty-of-karlowitz, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Tanzimat reforms
claims.summary: A wave of modernising reforms reorganised Ottoman law, taxation, education and the military in an effort to halt the empire's decline and integrate its diverse subjects.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1839-the-tanzimat-reforms, claim TL:TUR:event:1839:the-tanzimat-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Young Turk Revolution
claims.summary: The Young Turk movement forced Sultan Abdülhamid II to restore the constitution, ushering in a turbulent constitutional era dominated by the Committee of Union and Progress.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1908-young-turk-revolution, claim TL:TUR:event:1908:young-turk-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Armenian Genocide
claims.summary: From 24 April 1915 the Ottoman government deported and massacred its Armenian population in death marches and killings across Anatolia and into the Syrian desert; most historians recognise these events as genocide, with deaths estimated from roughly 600,000 to 1.5 million.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1915-the-armenian-genocide, claim TL:TUR:event:1915:the-armenian-genocide, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gallipoli campaign
claims.summary: Ottoman forces repelled an Allied attempt to seize the Dardanelles; the defence brought the officer Mustafa Kemal to national prominence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1915-gallipoli-campaign, claim TL:TUR:event:1915:gallipoli-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Sèvres
claims.summary: The Allied treaty with the defeated Ottoman government proposed partitioning Anatolia among Greece, Armenia, Italy, France and others; rejected by the nationalists, it triggered the War of Independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1920-treaty-of-sevres, claim TL:TUR:event:1920:treaty-of-sevres, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turkish War of Independence
claims.summary: Mustafa Kemal led a national resistance and a new Grand National Assembly in Ankara, defeating Greek, Armenian and French forces and ending the Allied occupation of Anatolia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1919-turkish-war-of-independence, claim TL:TUR:event:1919:turkish-war-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Lausanne
claims.summary: Replacing the Treaty of Sèvres, the Lausanne treaty secured international recognition of Turkey's sovereignty and borders, the legal foundation of the modern state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1923-treaty-of-lausanne, claim TL:TUR:event:1923:treaty-of-lausanne, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of the caliphate
claims.summary: The Grand National Assembly abolished the Ottoman caliphate and separated religion from the state, a cornerstone of Atatürk's secular reforms; a new constitution followed in April 1924.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1924-abolition-of-the-caliphate, claim TL:TUR:event:1924:abolition-of-the-caliphate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The alphabet and language reforms
claims.summary: Turkey replaced the Arabic script with a new Latin-based Turkish alphabet in 1928, part of reforms that sharply raised literacy and reoriented the nation toward Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1928-the-alphabet-and-language-reforms, claim TL:TUR:event:1928:the-alphabet-and-language-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First multiparty election
claims.summary: The Democrat Party won a landslide in the 1950 election, ending nearly three decades of one-party rule and marking Turkey's first peaceful transfer of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1950-first-multiparty-election, claim TL:TUR:event:1950:first-multiparty-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turkey joins NATO
claims.summary: Turkey became a member of NATO in 1952, cementing its strategic alignment with the West throughout the Cold War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-1952-turkey-joins-nato, claim TL:TUR:event:1952:turkey-joins-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Registered at the UN as 'Türkiye'
claims.summary: At the government's request, the United Nations registered the country's official name as 'Türkiye' in June 2022, replacing 'Turkey' in international usage.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Türkiye: From Neolithic Çatalhöyük and the Hittites through Byzantium and the Ottomans to Atatürk's republic.", terralore.co/country/TUR/chronicle#ev-2022-registered-at-the-un-as-turkiye, claim TL:TUR:event:2022:registered-at-the-un-as-turkiye, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
